Can Rangers extend their impressive run and pile the pressure on Celtic by moving to the top of the Premiership? Martin Dowden, Ewan Murray and Scott Allan assess why Derek McInnes' side have turned their season around and what to expect against Kilmarnock. There's also a first look at Marink Reedijk's Hibernian as he takes charge at Dundee United. Can a new manager spark an instant revival at Easter Road? articles.title: Retail dal prices surge by Rs 20-30 a kg across Mumbai Metropolitan Region
articles.summary: Retail dal prices in Mumbai Metropolitan Region jump Rs 20-30/kg as Vashi APMC wholesale rates rise on shortages, drought, higher costs and festive demand.
articles.body: NAVI MUMBAI: Prices of major pulses have risen by Rs 10-20 per kg in Vashi APMC wholesale market in recent weeks amid supply shortages, deficient monsoon rainfall, drought conditions, higher logistics costs and festive demand. Retail prices have increased by Rs 20-30 per kg.Pulse prices at the wholesale market rose by an average of Rs 15 from the previous month because of tight local supplies.Grain, Rice and Oilseeds Merchants’ Association (GROMA) president Bhimji Bhanushali said lower food grain arrivals followed drought conditions across Maharashtra. Wholesale price increases were being reflected in retail markets, where restrictions were limited, he said. Rohan Sawant, a consumer, said the recent hike in prices has disturbed the kitchen budget badly. Wholesale chana prices climbed from Rs 72 to Rs 82 per kg over the past month, while retail prices increased from Rs 110 to Rs 130. Tur prices rose from Rs 90 to Rs 105 per kg at APMC, while retail tur dal averaged about Rs 150 per kg, up from Rs 120 in Mumbai Metropolitan Region. Wholesale moong dal prices increased from Rs 95 to Rs 105 per kg, while retail prices averaged Rs 140.A wholesaler said prices could continue rising because of production losses in growing regions across Maharashtra and elsewhere in the country. Bhanushali said major pulse-producing states received below-average rainfall during the June-Sept monsoon, prompting drought declarations in parts of Karnataka and Maharashtra. Millers and stockists had also increased inventories before the festive season, while annual increases in minimum support prices affected selling prices. APMC grain market director Nilesh Veera said premium Kolam rice prices had risen from Rs 50 to Rs 60 per kg over the past fortnight, while basmati rice prices were also affected. Basmati rice prices rose by an average of Rs 5 per kg, while wheat and millet prices remained unchanged. articles.title: Proteína vegetal ou animal? Entenda diferença para ganho de músculos | G1
articles.standfirst: Especialistas explicam que a diferença principal está na composição nutricional de cada grupo.
articles.summary: Especialistas explicam que a diferença principal está na composição nutricional de cada grupo.
articles.body:
Em meio à popularização de dietas hiperproteicas e suplementos, uma dúvida continua aparecendo nos consultórios e nas academias: afinal, existe diferença entre proteína animal e vegetal quando o objetivo é ganhar massa muscular?

Especialistas ouvidos pelo Globo Repórter explicam que tanto as fontes animais quanto as vegetais podem fazer parte de uma alimentação voltada para a manutenção e o ganho de músculos. A principal diferença está na composição nutricional de cada grupo de alimentos e na forma como eles são combinados na dieta.

Segundo a nutricionista Alice, da USP, cada tipo de proteína tem características próprias e pode trazer vantagens diferentes dependendo dos objetivos e das condições de saúde de cada pessoa.

Proteína vegetal ou animal? Entenda diferença para ganho de músculos — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

As proteínas de origem animal, presentes em alimentos como carnes, ovos, leite e derivados, costumam ter uma composição de aminoácidos mais equilibrada. Já as proteínas vegetais também contêm os nove aminoácidos essenciais, mas em proporções diferentes.

Por isso, especialistas recomendam variar e combinar alimentos de origem vegetal para garantir um perfil nutricional mais completo. Um exemplo clássico é a combinação de arroz e feijão, tradicional na mesa dos brasileiros. Juntos, eles fornecem aminoácidos complementares e ajudam a formar uma proteína de melhor qualidade nutricional.

A cozinheira vegetariana Talita Flor destaca que essa combinação já faz parte da cultura alimentar brasileira.

“Eu sempre gosto de dizer que, para um brasileiro, ser vegetariano é muito mais fácil, porque a gente tem essa tradição do arroz e feijão, que já traz essa proteína completa”, afirma.

A resposta depende menos da origem da proteína e mais do conjunto da alimentação, da quantidade consumida ao longo do dia e da prática de exercícios físicos.

Para ilustrar essa questão, foram apresentados dois pratos diferentes: um com peixe e outro com proteína de soja. Apesar de utilizarem fontes distintas, ambos continham cerca de 25 gramas de proteína.

Proteína vegetal ou animal? Entenda diferença — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Segundo a nutricionista Alice, a escolha entre proteína animal e vegetal deve considerar também outros aspectos da saúde.

“Cada proteína carrega a sua importância. Nas proteínas de origem animal, como característica, elas carregam muito mais gordura saturada. Já as proteínas de origem vegetal têm uma quantidade maior de fibra”, explica.

As fibras, por exemplo, ajudam no funcionamento do intestino e aumentam a sensação de saciedade. Já alimentos de origem animal podem exigir mais atenção em pessoas com risco aumentado para doenças cardiovasculares.

Exercício continua sendo o principal fator

Especialistas reforçam que nenhuma proteína, seja animal ou vegetal, é capaz de promover ganho muscular sozinha.

O nutricionista e fisiologista do exercício Hamilton Roschel, da USP, afirma que o principal estímulo para o crescimento muscular continua sendo o treinamento de força.

“O grande gatilho para o aumento da massa e da força muscular é o exercício físico. A proteína é um complemento com uma magnitude de efeito bastante menor do que as pessoas concebem normalmente”, diz.

Segundo ele, existe um descompasso entre a expectativa criada em torno das proteínas e o impacto real que elas têm no desenvolvimento muscular.

articles.title: Feriado terá ciclone no Sul, chuva em SP e calor de até 40°C | G1
articles.standfirst: Frente fria deve aumentar a chuva no Sudeste e em Mato Grosso do Sul até segunda-feira (12). Norte e Nordeste terão predomínio de sol, mas algumas áreas ainda podem registrar pancadas fortes.
articles.summary: Frente fria deve aumentar a chuva em São Paulo até segunda-feira (12), e temporais atingem o Sul. Norte, Nordeste e parte do Centro-Oeste terão sol e calor intenso.
articles.body:
Tempo nublado ao redor do Santuário Nacional de Aparecida, no interior de SP. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

O feriado prolongado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida , celebrado na próxima segunda-feira (12), deve ser marcado por temporais no Sul, pancadas de chuva em parte do Sudeste e calor intenso em boa parte do Brasil.

No Sul, a formação de um novo ciclone extratropical deve provocar chuva forte e rajadas de vento durante o fim de semana.

Em São Paulo, a chegada de uma frente fria no domingo (11) deve aumentar as condições para pancadas de chuva, principalmente na segunda-feira, quando pode chover desde a manhã em algumas áreas do estado.

Já no Centro-Oeste, no Norte e no Nordeste, o sol deve predominar, e as temperaturas podem alcançar ou superar os 40°C em algumas localidades.

Segundo a Climatempo, o ciclone deve se formar no sábado (10), entre o Rio Grande do Sul e o Uruguai.

No domingo, o sistema estará sobre o Oceano Atlântico, próximo ao litoral gaúcho. A previsão é que ele perca força e se afaste da costa durante a segunda-feira.

"O início do feriado prolongado deve ser marcado por temporais no sábado (10), principalmente em Mato Grosso do Sul, no Paraná e em algumas áreas de Santa Catarina e do Rio Grande do Sul", diz César Soares, meteorologista da Climatempo.

"Mas essa chuva também deve se espalhar para outras áreas ao longo do domingo. Nesse dia, a frente fria deve mudar o tempo e aumentar as condições para chuva no litoral de São Paulo, onde há previsão de pancadas que podem ser um pouco mais fortes".

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia ( Inmet ) emitiu um aviso vermelho, de grande perigo, para tempestades entre sexta-feira (9) e sábado (10), abrangendo o oeste e sudoeste do Paraná, o centro e oeste de Santa Catarina e o noroeste e norte do Rio Grande do Sul. Há possibilidade de chuva intensa, rajadas fortes e queda de granizo.

Nas outras regiões do país, o calor forte deve predominar. O ar quente e seco vai manter as temperaturas elevadas em boa parte do interior do país, principalmente no Tocantins, Piauí, Maranhão, norte de Goiás e áreas de Mato Grosso e Minas Gerais.

Apesar do predomínio de sol, o feriado não será inteiramente seco nessas regiões. No oeste da Região Norte, as pancadas devem atingir principalmente Acre, Rondônia e Amazonas.

No litoral do Nordeste, a previsão também indica chuva passageira em algumas cidades.

🌦️ Veja os principais destaques para o feriado de 12 de outubro:

Sul: formação de ciclone extratropical provoca temporais e rajadas de até 70 km/h no fim de semana; chuva continua no Paraná e em Santa Catarina na segunda-feira (12);

Sudeste: frente fria aumenta a chuva em São Paulo, principalmente no feriado; Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais e Espírito Santo terão predomínio de sol e calor;

Centro-Oeste: calor predomina em Goiás, Mato Grosso e Distrito Federal, mas Mato Grosso do Sul terá pancadas mais frequentes e risco de temporais;

Nordeste: sol e calor na maior parte da região, e temperaturas próximas dos 40°C no interior; litoral pode registrar chuva passageira;

Norte: calor intenso, principalmente no Tocantins e no Pará, e pancadas de chuva mais frequentes no Acre, em Rondônia e no Amazonas.

No Sudeste, São Paulo deve concentrar a chuva mais forte durante o feriado prolongado. Na capital paulista, esta sexta-feira deve ter sol pela manhã e pancadas a partir da tarde, que podem vir acompanhadas de raios.

No sábado (10) e no domingo (11), o calor continua, com máximas próximas dos 30°C e possibilidade de chuva no fim do dia. Na segunda-feira (12), a chuva deve começar mais cedo e atingir também o litoral paulista.

No litoral, a previsão indica pancadas mais fortes entre Iguape e Peruíbe. Já na Baixada Santista e no Litoral Norte, o sol deve aparecer por mais tempo no sábado e no domingo, antes do aumento da chuva.

No Vale do Paraíba, Aparecida (SP) deve ter calor de até 32°C e pancadas de chuva à tarde e à noite, inclusive na segunda-feira, feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida.

No Rio de Janeiro, o sol e o calor devem predominar no fim de semana, com máximas de até 34°C na capital. Há possibilidade de chuva isolada, principalmente no sul fluminense e na região serrana.

Na segunda-feira, as pancadas devem atingir a cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ) à noite, e a máxima deve cair para cerca de 30°C.

Em Minas Gerais, o tempo deve seguir quente, com máximas próximas dos 31°C em Belo Horizonte (MG) e possibilidade de pancadas isoladas no domingo e na segunda-feira.

No Sul de Minas e na Zona da Mata, pode chover em alguns momentos. Já no norte e no oeste do estado, as temperaturas podem chegar aos 40°C.

No Espírito Santo, o sol e o calor devem predominar durante o feriado. Vitória (ES) pode registrar máximas entre 30°C e 33°C, e o interior pode chegar aos 35°C. Há possibilidade de chuva isolada no sul capixaba.

Mapa mostra previsão de chuva para esta quinta (09/10) em todo o Brasil. — Foto: CPTEC/Inpe

No Sul, a sexta-feira (9) deve ter chuva forte e risco de temporais nos três estados, principalmente no oeste da região. As pancadas mais intensas devem atingir o norte do Rio Grande do Sul, o centro e oeste de Santa Catarina e o oeste e sudoeste do Paraná.

No sábado (10), a formação de um ciclone extratropical próximo à costa gaúcha pode provocar rajadas de vento entre 50 e 70 km/h, inclusive em áreas sem chuva.

Em Porto Alegre (RS), a chuva deve perder força ao longo do fim de semana, e a máxima pode cair de 23°C na sexta para 18°C na segunda-feira (12). Em Florianópolis (SC) e Curitiba (PR), as pancadas devem continuar durante o feriado, com risco de temporais.

No domingo (11), a chuva deve diminuir em boa parte do Rio Grande do Sul, mas pode voltar a ganhar força em Santa Catarina e no Paraná durante a tarde e a noite.

Na segunda-feira (12), a chuva deve continuar em Santa Catarina e no Paraná. No território gaúcho, as pancadas ficam mais concentradas na serra, no norte e no extremo sul. As temperaturas devem cair, mas sem previsão de frio intenso na maior parte da região.

No Centro-Oeste, o sol e o calor devem predominar durante o feriado, principalmente em Goiás e no Distrito Federal. Brasília (DF) pode chegar aos 34°C, e Goiânia (GO), aos 36°C, sem previsão de chuva significativa.

Em Mato Grosso, o calor também continua, mas há previsão de pancadas isoladas. Cuiabá (MT) pode registrar 37°C e chuva forte no sábado (10), principalmente à tarde.

Já em Mato Grosso do Sul, a passagem de uma frente fria deve aumentar o risco de temporais durante o fim de semana. Em Campo Grande (MS), a máxima pode cair de 32°C na sexta-feira (9) para 27°C no sábado.

No domingo (11) e na segunda-feira (12), há risco de chuva forte, ventos intensos e granizo, principalmente no oeste e sul do estado.

Temperaturas mínimas previstas para esta sexta (09/10) em todo o Brasil. — Foto: CPTEC/Inpe

No Nordeste, o sol e o calor devem predominar durante o feriado, principalmente no interior. As temperaturas podem chegar aos 40°C em áreas do Maranhão, Piauí e Bahia. Em Teresina (PI), a máxima pode alcançar 41°C na sexta-feira (9).

No litoral, há previsão de chuva passageira, principalmente em João Pessoa (PB), Recife (PE) e Maceió (AL). Nas demais capitais, o tempo deve ficar mais firme, com períodos de sol e calor.

No Norte, o calor deve continuar, com pancadas mais fortes no Acre, em Rondônia e no Amazonas, principalmente à tarde e à noite. Em Porto Velho (RO), a temperatura pode chegar aos 37°C, e há risco de temporal no domingo (11).

Em Manaus (AM), as máximas podem alcançar 38°C, mas a chuva deve ser menos frequente na capital. No Pará e no Tocantins, o calor pode chegar aos 40°C, enquanto Belém (PA), Macapá (AP) e Boa Vista (RR) devem ter predomínio de sol.

Na terça-feira (13), a chuva deve continuar em parte do Centro-Sul, principalmente em São Paulo e Santa Catarina. Na capital paulista, a máxima pode cair para 26°C, enquanto Florianópolis (SC) deve registrar até 19°C.

No Centro-Oeste, Brasília (DF) pode ter pancadas à noite. Já no Nordeste e no Norte, o calor deve continuar, com possibilidade de chuva passageira em algumas áreas.

articles.title: Antipetismo vs. antibolsonarismo: o voto 'do contra' que pode decidir a eleição - O Assunto #1822 | G1
articles.standfirst: A força do antipetismo e do antibolsonarismo ajudou a levar Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula (PT) ao 2º turno, mas agora os dois têm desafios diferentes.
articles.summary: A força do antipetismo e do antibolsonarismo ajudou a levar Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula (PT) ao 2º turno, mas agora os dois têm desafios diferentes.
articles.body:
Durante toda a campanha eleitoral do 1º turno, os dois candidatos apareceram na dianteira das pesquisas de intenção de voto eram os mesmos que carregavam, de longe, os maiores índices de rejeição. A força do antipetismo e do antibolsonarismo ajudou a levar Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula (PT) ao 2º turno, mas agora os dois têm desafios diferentes. A primeira pesquisa Datafolha desta nova fase da eleição aponta Flávio com 52% dos votos válidos (49% dos totais), contra 48% (45% dos totais) de Lula. Agora, a campanha do presidente busca reforçar a rejeição ao filho de Jair Bolsonaro para tentar uma virada, enquanto a do senador precisa consolidar a vantagem conquistada no último domingo (4).

Neste episódio, Natuza Nery recebe o cientista político Carlos Melo. Carlos explica o surgimento e a consolidação dos fenômenos do antipetismo e do antibolsonarismo e analisa o que os dois candidatos buscam fazer para reduzir suas rejeições e aumentar a do adversário.

Convidado: Carlos Melo, cientista político e professor do Insper.

articles.title: Macaé Moto Week 2026 começa nesta sexta-feira no Parque de Exposições | G1
articles.standfirst: Maior festival do gênero na região reúne 32 atrações musicais, show do Capital Inicial, praça de alimentação e mais de 200 motoclubes.
articles.summary: Maior festival do gênero na região reúne 32 atrações musicais, show do Capital Inicial, praça de alimentação e mais de 200 motoclubes.
articles.body:
Parque de Exposições Latiff Mussi recebe estrutura completa com dois palcos, camping e praça de alimentação — Foto: Arquivo Secom

O Macaé Moto Week 2026, considerado o maior festival de motociclismo e rock da Região Norte Fluminense, chega ao Parque de Exposições Latiff Mussi entre os dias 9 e 12 de outubro, durante o feriado prolongado. Realizado pela Prefeitura de Macaé e produzido pela empresa MMW, o evento tem entrada gratuita, acompanhada de uma campanha solidária com arrecadação de 1 kg de alimento não perecível para os programas sociais da Paróquia Santo Antônio. A estimativa de público é de 15 mil a 20 mil pessoas por dia, com a presença de cerca de 200 motoclubes de várias regiões do país.

A estrutura do festival foi planejada para atender toda a família, oferecendo área para camping, espaço para motorhome, praça de alimentação e área de convivência. A grade de programação conta com 32 atrações musicais divididas em 40 apresentações entre a Arena MMW e o Palco Loud, além de shows de manobras radicais no sábado (10), no domingo (11) e na segunda-feira (12). O grande destaque da edição é o show nacional da banda Capital Inicial, agendado para o domingo (11), às 23h30, na Arena MMW.

A abertura oficial ocorre na sexta-feira (9), às 18h30, na Arena MMW, seguida pelos shows de Tutti Fruti (20h), Faixa Etária (21h45) e Segredo de Estado (23h30). No Palco Loud, a sexta-feira terá Faya (19h), Makako Velhu (21h) e Shout (23h). No sábado (10), a Arena MMW recebe Equalize (14h), SR Chow (15h30), Improvável (17h), Filhos da Maldita (18h30), Manobras Radicais (19h), Faya (20h), VMAX (21h45) e Cilindrada (23h30); enquanto o Palco Loud terá Isonomia (15h), Madre Vinil (17h), Back in Blues (19h), Mr Highway (21h) e 70 Milhas (23h).

No domingo (11), a movimentação na Arena MMW começa às 12h, com apresentações da Banda Joker (14h), Makako Velhu (15h30), Arken (17h), Omnia Vincit (18h30), Manobras Radicais (19h) e Grotescos (20h), antecedendo a atração principal, Capital Inicial (23h30).

No Palco Loud, tocam Lab of Souls (15h), Vibe da Cidade (17h), Tomarock (19h), Gato du Mato (21h) e Violence Division (23h). No encerramento, na segunda-feira (12), a Arena MMW traz Back in Blues (14h), Freemind (15h30), Manobras Radicais (17h), Mustang Velho (18h30) e 4G (19h); e o Palco Loud apresenta VMAX (15h), Arken (17h), Basalt (19h) e Solene (21h). Expositores de artigos de motociclismo, vestuário e acessórios ainda podem se cadastrar pelo Direct do Instagram ( @macaemotoweek ).

articles.summary: Daniela, Moçambique e Açores estão entre os novos destinos com selo Bandeira Azul em SC, que mantém a liderança nacional em qualidade ambiental para 2026/2027.
articles.body:
Seis novas praias e uma marina de Santa Catarina foram reconhecidas pelo programa Bandeira Azul , selo que destaca destinos no quesito ambiental. O resultado da temporada 2026/2027 foi divulgado nesta semana.

🏖️ As novidades da lista, considerada o "Oscar das Praias", incluem três destinos em Florianópolis , dois no Norte e um no Sul do estado.

🔎 Para obter o selo Bandeira Azul, os locais precisam cumprir 38 critérios anuais obrigatórios, divididos em quatro áreas principais: qualidade da água, gestão ambiental, segurança e serviços, e educação e informação ambiental. O processo de avaliação inclui etapa com júri nacional e validação final pela Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE), na Dinamarca.

Veja abaixo as praias catarinenses que estreiam na lista da Bandeira Azul.

A Praia da Daniela, localizada no Norte da Ilha de Santa Catarina, em Florianópolis, tem mar calmo e quente. É uma boa escolha para famílias.

A praia também já teve registro de jacarés. Em um dos registros, um jacaré foi visto atravessando a faixa de areia e passando no meio de banhistas.

Praia da Daniela, no Norte da Ilha, em Florianópolis. — Foto: Robson Boamorte/Globoesporte.com

🏝️ Praia do Moçambique, Florianópolis (SC)

O mar da Praia do Moçambique é bastante agitado, por isso, é preciso cuidado. Há correnteza e é um local procurado pelos surfistas.

Não é uma praia muito badalada, portanto é um lugar ótimo para apreciar a natureza em grandes interferências.

Onda na Praia do Moçambique, em Florianópolis — Foto: Cadu Fagundes/Divulgação

A Praia dos Açores é um dos refúgios mais preservados e tranquilos do Sul da Ilha de Santa Catarina. Situada a cerca de 30 quilômetros do Centro, ela fica estrategicamente posicionada entre a badalada Praia do Pântano do Sul e a isolada Praia da Solidão.

Praia dos Açores, em Florianópolis — Foto: SeturSC/Divulgação

🏝️ Praia de Itapema do Norte - Trecho Beira Mar III, Itapoá (SC)

A praia conta com uma ampla faixa de areia dourada e águas claras. Por ser uma região de mar aberto, apresenta águas limpas e ondas que variam de médias a grandes, sendo muito convidativa para banho e esportes náuticos.

Praia de Itapoá — Foto: Prefeitura de Itapoá/Divulgação

A Praia do Mar Grosso é a mais famosa, movimentada e estruturada de Laguna, no Litoral Sul de Santa Catarina.

Possui cerca de 3 quilômetros de extensão e uma larga faixa de areia clara e fina. Em vários trechos, dunas e cômoros com vegetação nativa formam uma barreira natural entre a avenida e a areia

Praia do Mar Grosso, Laguna — Foto: Prefeitura de Laguna/Divulgação

🏝️Praia do Molhe, São Francisco do Sul (SC)

A Praia do Molhe, em São Francisco do Sul, é um refúgio natural cercado por morros e Mata Atlântica. Com águas cristalinas e areia clara, ela mistura trechos calmos e áreas com boas ondas para o surfe.

O acesso principal é feito por uma curta trilha a pé, o que garante uma atmosfera sossegada de "praia secreta".

Praia do Mar Grosso, Laguna — Foto: Prefietura de Laguna/Divulgação

Além das seis estreantes, o estado conta com a volta da Praia do Cerro , em Barra Velha , que retornou à lista dos locais certificados nesta temporada.

Com as adesões e renovações de destinos já premiados anteriormente, Santa Catarina mantém a liderança nacional do programa ecológico, somando 38 pontos reconhecidos — entre 33 praias e cinco marinas. ( Veja a lista completa das praias contempladas aqui )

No cenário nacional, o Brasil teve 75 candidaturas aprovadas (63 praias e 12 marinas) em sete estados, o que representa um crescimento de 25% em relação à temporada anterior.

Depois de Santa Catarina, os estados com maior número de selos são Rio de Janeiro , com 20 locais, e Bahia, com 7.

articles.title: This old CIA airfield is now a Chinese base
articles.summary: The Ban Keun base in Laos used to be used by the CIA-operated Air America during the Vietnam War, as a logistics and support hub for secret operations in the region.
articles.body: China’s military has opened a new outpost on a site in northwestern Laos which was once a Vietnam-era CIA airfield. The base, about 40 miles north of the capital Vientiane and just 25 miles from the nearest border with Thailand, comprises the China-Laos Joint Support and Training Center at Ban Keun Airport, and the China-Laos Friendship Aviation Academy. It began operations on September 29, according to an announcement from China’s Defense Ministry. Photos obtained by CNN from satellite imagery and intelligence platform Vantor show a 6,500-foot-long (2,000-meter-long) runway, taxiway and parking apron for 22 aircraft have been completed at the base since December. The facilities are “designed to help Laos strengthen the training and development of its air force pilots and will be jointly maintained by both sides,” the Defense Ministry statement said. Eight aircraft – possibly Hongdu JL-8 jets, a two-seat training and light-attack aircraft – are visible in the satellite photos. The facilities are “not directed against any third party and are conducive to further strengthening practical cooperation between the two militaries and maintaining regional peace and stability,” the ministry said. To date, China has only one official overseas base, an installation in Djibouti, northeast Africa, that opened in 2017. It also funded a major expansion of Cambodia’s Ream Naval Base on the Gulf of Thailand, which it operates jointly with the Cambodian military. A new pier there, large enough to handle the PLA Navy’s aircraft carriers, has raised concerns about Beijing’s intentions in the region. But Cambodia’s government maintains Ream is open to others, including the US Navy, which had a littoral combat ship call there in January. The Ban Keun base in Laos used to be used by the CIA-operated Air America during the Vietnam War, as a logistics and support hub for secret operations in the region. But China’s move there – while symbolic – doesn’t signal any major shift in the US-China power balance, analysts said. Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies in Singapore, said Thursday it’s hard to see any threat to US forces in the region from the base. “This runway is not a dagger pointed at the heart of anything,” Thompson said. “I struggle to think of a scenario where (China would) want to generate aircraft sorties from there,” he said, noting its location near Thailand, a major non-NATO ally of the US. Rachel Vandenbrink, a senior analyst at the Australian Strategic Policy Institute, told Reuters that China’s selection of Ban Keun “is likely more about a target of opportunity than filling an obvious operational need.” “Laos does have some geostrategic value as an accessible foothold in mainland Southeast Asia, given its shared border with China and infrastructure links, including (its) railway,” Vandenbrink told the news agency. CNN’s Isaac Yee contributed to this report.

articles.title: UN extends Darfur arms embargo, blocks broader Sudan sanctions proposal
articles.summary: Russia and China block US efforts to expand the Darfur arms embargo to cover all of Sudan amid ongoing conflict.
articles.body:
The United Nations Security Council extended the arms embargo on Sudan’s Darfur region by two months but failed to agree on a US proposal to widen it to the whole country, after permanent members Russia and China opposed it.

The 15-member council unanimously adopted Resolution 2830 on Thursday, extending the sanctions regime until December 11 to allow more time for negotiations.

It also extended the mandate of the panel of experts that monitors the measures until January 11, 2027. The UN described the text as a short-term “technical rollover”, after the regime was last renewed for one month on September 11.

The sanctions were first imposed in 2005 under Resolution 1591.

The council set up an arms embargo on armed actors in Darfur , a travel ban and an asset freeze on designated individuals and entities, and a five-member panel of experts to monitor them.

Despite weeks of discussion, the United States failed to secure approval to expand the embargo. Russia and China have argued for keeping the existing regime.

“The current sanctions regime is over 20 years outdated, and is insufficient to address the realities of the war today,” US Ambassador Jeff Bartos told the council last month, urging it to “expand the arms embargo across the entire territory of Sudan”.

Russia’s deputy UN ambassador, Anna Evstigneeva, said at the time: “We will not allow even a hint of broadening the restrictions by the council on Sudan.”

Sudan’s UN ambassador, Al-Harith Mohamed, argued that a total embargo goes against the UN Charter’s guarantee of the right to self-defence.

The war between the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which began in April 2023, has killed at least 59,000 people, though aid groups warn the toll could be far higher .

It has also displaced about 13 million people and pushed parts of the country into famine.

The army holds central and eastern Sudan, while the RSF controls Darfur in the west and parts of the south.

Darfur, a region about the size of Spain, has seen some of the worst violence, with displacement camps attacked and repeated ethnic massacres killing thousands at a time.

articles.title: Protests, debate follow death of Maricarmen, 87, Spain protest symbol
articles.summary: Thousands of protesters honour Maricarmen Abascal’s life, while tributes in Spanish parliament spark debate.
articles.body:
Thousands of Spaniards protested outside Spain’s parliament after the death of Maria del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction ignited nationwide protests and sparked a snap general election .

Meanwhile, tributes to Abascal were debated within the legislature as lawmakers accused each other of exploiting the case ahead of the election.

Maricarmen Abascal died on Wednesday after being hospitalised for severe anxiety and exhaustion since her eviction on a stretcher from her Madrid home on September 23.

While in the hospital, she reached a deal to return to her home but died before she could return. No cause of death has been announced.

“They killed her through heartbreak,” Diana, a demonstrator, told Al Jazeera. “Taking an 87-year-old woman out of her home after she had lived in the same house for 70 years, that is killing someone.”

Diana joined thousands of protesters outside Spain’s parliament.

Outside Abascal’s building, mourners left flowers, candles, handwritten notes and children’s drawings.

“They’re not deaths; they’re murders,” protesters chanted as they walked from a protest camp in the central Puerta del Sol square to Abascal’s former home on Thursday.

Protests over home shortages and surging rents following her eviction prompted Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call a snap general election for November 29 after parliament failed to pass emergency housing measures.

Tributes to Abascal in the Madrid region’s legislature caused arguments as lawmakers accused each other of exploiting the case ahead of the election.

Alberto Nunez Feijoo, leader of the conservative opposition People’s Party (PP), accused Sanchez and the Socialists of trying to exploit the housing crisis for political gain ahead of the election.

“We will not allow this attempt to manipulate the emotions of the Spanish people; all of this has happened during their eight years in government. It won’t fly,” Feijoo said.

The PP, which holds absolute majorities in the Madrid regional and local assemblies, refused to observe a minute of silence in her honour. Instead, hard-left deputies staged one outside City Hall and gave Abascal a 60-second standing ovation during a tense debate in the regional assembly, while PP lawmakers remained seated with folded arms.

Left-leaning parties criticised conservatives for rejecting legislation in parliament aimed at curbing soaring rental prices.

A survey carried out in June and published by state pollster CIS on Thursday found that 76.3 percent of Spaniards supported intervention in the market to guarantee access to housing, while 79 percent believed the right to housing should take precedence over treating homes as a market commodity.

Ombudsman Angel Gabilondo said addressing the housing crisis would require greater commitment from all levels of government.

He said his office was preparing a housing report and reiterated proposals to expand public housing, restrict tourist rentals, increase rent assistance and strengthen protections against evictions for vulnerable households.

articles.title: 2 foreign nationals breach UK base housing key US, NATO intel hub amid $556M expansion
articles.summary: The Latvian men were arrested under the National Security Act 2023 after breaching a fence at RAF Molesworth, prompting a major counterterrorism investigation.
articles.body: Two Latvian nationals legally living in the United Kingdom were arrested under Section 4 of Britain's National Security Act of 2023 Thursday after allegedly breaching a perimeter fence at RAF Molesworth, a sensitive British military base housing critical U.S. and NATO intelligence operations, Reuters reported. The arrests triggered a major counterterrorism investigation into the security breach at the strategic installation, which serves as a central intelligence hub supporting American military commanders across Europe and Africa. The base is also undergoing a $556.5 million expansion centered on the Joint Intelligence Analysis Complex (JIAC), a location designed to consolidate 20 intelligence facilities and accommodate more than 1,000 personnel, according to reports. IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY The suspects, ages 32 and 36, were discovered inside the base around 2 a.m. Thursday after an extensive security sweep. Ministry of Defense Police officers conducting routine patrols first raised the alarm around 10 p.m. Wednesday after finding an abandoned vehicle near the perimeter. Bomb disposal specialists cleared the vehicle before armed officers discovered a fence breach and located the men inside. Initially detained on suspicion of trespass and criminal damage, both men were arrested again under the National Security Act for allegedly entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the United Kingdom. They remain in custody as counterterrorism detectives execute search warrants at two residential properties in nearby Peterborough. Managed by the U.S. Air Force's 423rd Air Base Group, RAF Molesworth is a nonflying installation dedicated to joint intelligence and command operations. It houses intelligence elements for U.S. European Command, U.S. Africa Command and the NATO Intelligence Fusion Centre. During World War II, the airfield was used by the U.S. 15th Bombardment Squadron. In 1973, the airfield was officially deactivated before transitioning into its current role as an intelligence center. Construction on the JIAC broke ground April 12, 2024, with onsite work beginning that spring. The facility is scheduled for completion in summer 2028. FOILED TERROR PLOT AT BOMBER BASE SIGNALS WIDER THREAT TO US MILITARY INSTALLATIONS: EXPERT A 2024 Defense Department release described the base development as part of the department's overall European Infrastructure Consolidation efforts. "It will combine 20 facilities and over 1,000 DIA personnel into one location. Among others, it will host members of the NATO Intelligence Fusion Centre, Battlefield Information Collection and Exploitation System, U.S. Africa Command, U.S. European Command and U.S. Air Force elements in a cross-agency, multi-mission collaboration." At the time, Defense Intelligence Agency Deputy Director Suzanne White said the facility would enable "the U.S. and allies’ shared mission of ‘outpacing our strategic competitors and addressing threats together wherever they may arise.’" The Defense Department designed the project with a two-stage procurement strategy, allowing stakeholder agencies to provide feedback and streamline scheduling requirements. Following the intrusion, U.S. European Command praised the swift British response. "We would also express our gratitude to the UK for the close partnership with U.S. forces on matters of security." British counterterrorism officials cautioned against drawing premature conclusions about possible espionage or terrorist motives. "We're very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites," Counterterrorism Policing London commander Helen Flanagan said. articles.title: ICE agent shoots man in New York City
articles.summary: The mayor of New York expressed outrage at the shooting which the Department of Homeland Security said happened during the arrest of a "criminal illegal alien".
articles.body:
A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot a man in the Bronx in New York City on Thursday.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which runs the agency, confirmed an ICE officer "discharged his weapon" during "a targeted enforcement operation... to arrest a criminal illegal alien".

In a statement, it added the man was alive and at a local hospital.

New York mayor Zohran Mamdani said it was an "unconscionable and incredibly serious situation".

"Early reports indicate agents surrounded him and a five-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds. We believe the child was physically unharmed," he said.

The BBC has approached DHS for comment about Mamdani's remarks.

Late on Thursday evening, New York Governor Kathy Hochul said she had spoken to President Donald Trump about the shooting and had expressed "outrage on behalf of New Yorkers".

"I also asked that any body camera footage of the shooting be released to the public so we can establish the facts and get to the truth."

Trump has not yet commented publicly on the shooting.

The DHS said the man, who has not been named by officials, was from the Dominican Republic and had "a prior criminal conviction for grand larceny, and multiple prior arrests for assault, robbery, possession of drugs, and weapons possession".

He was arrested by police officers in New York in December 2023 and released "a few days later", according to the DHS statement.

It also claimed he was associated with the Trinitarios, described by the US justice department as a transnational criminal group.

Mamdani, meanwhile, said he would ask Trump to end ICE enforcement actions in the city.

"I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorise our communities," he wrote on X on Thursday evening.

New York, which is a Democratic stronghold, is one of several American cities that bars its police officers from assisting with federal immigration enforcement.

A group of protesters gathered at the scene on Thursday evening, chanting "we want justice" and "ICE off our streets now".

There have been several high-profile shootings involving ICE officers this year, including one which caused the death of Renee Good in Minneapolis in January.

articles.title: Key takeaways from US Senate debate in Michigan between El-Sayed, Rogers
articles.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers are locked in a toss-up race for the US Senate.
articles.body:
The leading candidates in Michigan’s heated Senate race have faced off in their first televised debate, with less than a month remaining before the United States midterm elections.

Thursday’s hour-long debate was a microcosm of how tense the toss-up race has become.

Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed, formerly the health director for Wayne County, repeatedly sought to paint his Republican adversary Mike Rogers as a yacht-owning millionaire out of touch with ordinary voters.

For his part, Rogers, a former member of the US House of Representatives, lobbed accusations at El-Sayed that he was soft on “terrorism” and had foreign sympathies.

The Michigan-born El-Sayed has repeatedly faced Islamophobic attacks while on the campaign trail, with Republican President Donald Trump labelling him an “extremist, terrorist sympathizer” whose history “goes back to the days of the Jihad”. If elected, El-Sayed would be the first Muslim member of the US Senate.

The two candidates spent much of their hour onstage together speaking over one another, as they exchanged pointed barbs.

“He can’t condemn a terrorist act that happened on our soil in the state of Michigan. He can’t bring himself to condemn –,” Rogers began, referencing a March attack on a synagogue.

“I did condemn it,” El-Sayed said, jumping in. “No, you did not,” Rogers replied, with El-Sayed quickly responding, “You make stuff up. You make stuff up.”

The Senate race in Michigan is considered key to the battle for control of the US Senate. Democrats are seeking to flip both chambers of Congress, but shifting control of the Senate will be a tougher prospect, given that only a third of its 100 seats are on the November 3 ballot.

Host Rick Albin at times struggled to keep the debate on track, as tensions rose.

“We’ve got dozens of questions we want to get to. You can’t litigate all of these with 14 different rebuttals, so please work with me,” Albin told the two candidates at one point.

Here are the key takeaways from the evening’s debate.

Rogers insinuates El-Sayed family ties to ‘terrorism watch list’

The ferocity of the debate was underscored by the high volume of ad hominem attacks the candidates deployed against each other.

But Rogers repeatedly pushed a series of attacks that seemed to centre on El-Sayed’s identity as a Muslim.

In response to a question about healthcare, Rogers said that El-Sayed has “taken money from individuals on his campaign who openly support Hamas, Hezbollah, al-Qaeda”.

Later, when asked about his position on surveillance by Flock cameras, Rogers argued that such technology has helped catch people suspected of terrorism. He then implied that El-Sayed’s concerns about the cameras were suggestive.

“Why would that bother you?” Rogers asked El-Sayed. “Well, if you have somebody in your family that might be on the terrorism watch list …”

El-Sayed interjected, seeming to dare Rogers to continue his thought.

“Are you going to go ahead and say that I’m a – go ahead and say it,” El-Sayed said. “You’ve been tiptoeing about it the whole time. Just say it. Just say it. Go ahead and say it.”

Muslim and Arab candidates in the US have frequently been subjected to Islamophobic attacks on the campaign trail, accusing them of support for “terrorism” and Islamic fundamentalism.

There were issues, however, on which both candidates found a measure of common ground.

Both Rogers and El-Sayed agreed the US-Israeli war against Iran should end, but they had opposite views on Washington’s relationship with Israel and its role in the conflict.

High gasoline prices and inflation, El-Sayed said, were directly caused by the Iran war, and he blamed the Trump administration for Iran’s decision to shut down the Strait of Hormuz, a critical trade route.

“This is what happens when you start wars you never should be fighting,” El-Sayed said. “We literally taught the Iranian regime that they have a choke on the Strait of Hormuz, and now we’re living in that reality.”

Rogers agreed that “we need [the war] to come to an end”, but he also justified the conflict, saying that Iran’s uranium enrichment programme had been “set back twenty years”, echoing a frequent White House talking point.

The Trump administration has argued that the war was necessary to prevent Iran from creating a nuclear weapon, a goal Tehran has long denied.

Rogers’s position led El-Sayed to accuse him of “cheerleading” for the war and the Trump administration.

Rogers backs continued Israel aid, El-Sayed calls for end

As part of the debate about US foreign policy, the candidates were also pressed on their positions about the US alliance with Israel.

The country is considered the largest overall recipient of US aid since World War II. From the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023 through September 2025, experts estimate that Israel received nearly $21.7bn in military aid.

El-Sayed has openly called for ending aid to Israel, and he has repeatedly denounced the conflict in Gaza as a genocide, in line with evaluations from United Nations experts and human rights watchdogs.

During the debate, he indicated he preferred US taxpayer dollars to be spent on domestic concerns like education and healthcare, rather than Israeli aid.

“He wants unconditional support for a foreign government,” El-Sayed said of Rogers. “I want unconditional support for kids in our schools, unconditional support for our healthcare, childcare.”

He also blamed Israel for the US military action in Iran. “I don’t want to be pushed into war by Israel, and I don’t want to be in war with Iran,” El-Sayed said.

Rogers, meanwhile, has joined most of his fellow Republicans in continuing to support aid for Israel. He argued that the country had “the right to defend itself in a very difficult neighbourhood”.

“Is there anything Israel could do that would lose your support?” the debate host asked.

“Listen, if they’re talking about using nuclear weapons, they would definitely lose my support,” Rogers replied.

Rogers calls immigration crackdown ‘not appropriate’

Another hot-button issue during the debate was Trump’s crackdown on immigration.

The Republican leader has pledged to carry out the largest mass deportation effort in US history, and his campaign has spurred human rights concerns.

When asked how they would approach the crackdown, both Rogers and El-Sayed agreed on tempering the militarised nature of the campaign.

In several cities, including Minneapolis, Minnesota, immigration authorities have been accused of racial profiling and using excessive force against immigrants and protesters, as well as violating their rights to due process.

Multiple fatal shootings have occurred during immigration enforcement operations, including the deaths of Renee Good and Alex Pretti in January.

Rogers indicated he would not have supported such confrontational operations, but he repeated a Trump claim that the raids were taking dangerous criminals off the streets.

“I think the public efforts in Minnesota were probably not appropriate,” Rogers said. “You always want to go in quiet, get the bad guy, get out of the neighbourhood for less problems. So that, to me, was something that they could have done differently.”

He later claimed that, under Trump, the country had seen “the largest decrease in murders ever recorded”.

El-Sayed, meanwhile, has previously voiced support for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), a key agency in Trump’s deportation campaign. He defended that stance on the debate stage.

“ICE right now is not about immigration enforcement. ICE is about terrorising our streets,” he said.

Candidates debate Canada trade war and tariffs

Donald Trump’s trade war with Canada, felt acutely in neighbouring Michigan, was another key topic of conversation.

El-Sayed depicted Rogers as an uncritical backer of Trump and his tariffs and tied him to past free trade deals such as the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which paved the way for companies to shift manufacturing facilities out of the US – though Rogers did not enter Congress until 2001, eight years after NAFTA passed.

“You did that, man. That was your policy. NAFTA, that was your policy,” said El-Sayed.

Rogers sought to distance himself from the current trade war but expressed support for a deal with Canada that would loosen some of Ottawa’s tariffs on US goods.

“I would like to see the deal made,” said Rogers, adding that high Canadian tariffs for US goods “should be eliminated”.

Both candidates tried to strike a balance between criticism of the economic fallout of the trade war and qualifying their support for more selective tariffs, favoured by some industries and labour unions as a means of protecting domestic jobs.

articles.title: Christa Pike case underscores prevalence of botched executions in US
articles.summary: Experts say methods such as lethal injection promise a more humane form of execution but are frequently marred by mishap
articles.body:
The botched execution of Christa Pike has sparked debate about the death penalty in the United States, where lethal injections, experts say, are frequently marred by mishaps and incompetence.

The attempted execution of Pike, a woman sentenced to death for her participation in the murder of a classmate when she was 18 years old, was called off after two doses of pentobarbital failed to kill her on September 30.

Witnesses reported that she continued to breathe, snore and lift parts of her body off the gurney to which she was strapped even after the lethal injections were administered. Pike’s lawyers said that she had regained consciousness at the hospital on October 6 but faces a long path to recovery.

Governor Bill Lee announced a pause on executions in the state and promised a “comprehensive, third-party review” of the incident, the second case this year in which Tennessee authorities have called off an execution after a failed lethal injection attempt.

The Tennessee Department of Correction declined to comment when asked by Al Jazeera why the execution attempt failed and whether it planned to try to execute Pike again.

While the case has attracted nationwide attention, experts say that botched execution attempts , largely carried out through lethal injection, are a disturbingly common feature of capital punishment in the US.

“This is an opportunity for everyone to stop and really carefully examine all of the ways in which this execution went wrong and to make good decisions about how to move forward, if we’re going to move forward with this method of execution,” said Robin Maher, the executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center, a nonprofit research group based in Washington, DC.

Of the various methods of execution in the US, lethal injection is by far the most common. It is also among the least reliable.

States such as Tennessee, Idaho, Alabama, Arizona, Texas and Oklahoma have all recorded at least one botched execution via lethal injection since 2022, and a survey of executions in the US between 1890 and 2010 found that lethal injections were botched at more than twice the rate of all other methods.

Researchers attribute the poor record of lethal injection to a number of factors, including the difficulty of carrying out what amounts to a medical procedure in a prison setting without access to qualified staff.

Major medical organisations bar members from assisting in executions on the basis that it violates their mandate to do no harm, meaning that prisons rely on staff members or officials with dubious credentials to carry out the procedure.

“Lethal injection has all of the delicacies of a medical procedure: all of the error-prone qualities, all of the need for precision. But it has been warped to fit the needs of execution settings,” said Corinna Barrett Lain, a professor at the University of Richmond School of Law and author of a book on lethal injection.

She explained that she has witnessed botched executions that drag on for hours and include prisoners being punctured with needles more than a dozen times. “It’s this really bad combination of a delicate procedure that is not performed in a delicate way.”

Pharmaceutical companies also restrict the use of their products in executions, meaning that some states acquire drugs used in lethal injection through facilities called compounding pharmacies.

Such pharmacies often prepare medications not manufactured commercially, and the drugs they produce are not as extensively scrutinised as mass-produced medications. Some states have also sought to stretch existing stockpiles of drugs used in lethal injections, though they can become expired or faulty.

The risks are compounded by the people the lethal injections are administered to.

Those on death row often spend years or even decades waiting for their execution. Since many are of an advanced age, they are more likely to have health issues that can further complicate the procedure.

Botched executions often feature failed attempts to locate a vein or set an IV line.

While state officials have yet to offer an explanation of why Pike’s execution failed, her lawyers had previously argued that she had small veins and a blood condition that were likely to complicate a lethal injection effort.

After the lethal injections, Pike’s lawyers described her arms as swollen and burned.

Maher, the head of the Death Penalty Information Center, said those symptoms suggest the injection may not have properly reached her bloodstream.

“Everyone has speculated that the drugs were administered to her but did not enter her bloodstream in sufficient amounts to kill her,” she said. “It’s likely that her veins were blown, or that the needle went through the vein.”

When the lethal injection drugs fail to be properly administered, executions can be drawn out and, in some cases, unnecessarily painful for prisoners.

After the first dose of pentobarbital was administered to her, Pike reportedly stated that she felt her arm was “about to burst open”.

In May, Tennessee also called off the execution of Tony Carruthers after staff struggled for more than 90 minutes to establish a backup IV line.

In February 2024, the state of Idaho likewise suspended the execution of Thomas Creech, a man in his 70s, after an execution team failed to properly insert an IV after eight attempts in his arms, legs and feet.

Despite such incidents, lethal injection has become the primary method of execution in 28 of the 29 states that still allow capital punishment, according to the National Conference of State Legislatures. The first execution via lethal injection occurred in Texas in 1982.

According to the Death Penalty Information Center, 39 people were killed by lethal injection in 2025, compared with five by lethal gas and three by firing squad. The last electrocution of a prisoner took place in 2020, and older methods such as hanging have not been employed since the 1990s.

Michael Radelet, a professor of sociology at the University of Colorado who has tracked botched executions, says that lethal injection has taken the place of older forms of execution that came to be seen as outdated and draconian.

Such methods also resulted in grim spectacles that distressed observers. Prisoners being electrocuted sometimes caught on fire or disturbed witnesses with the smell of burning flesh.

“Lethal injection is relatively new, but it’s part of a long-term trend going back hundreds of years in search of a more ‘humane’ method of execution,” Radelet told Al Jazeera.

But he added that the method’s promise of a more peaceful and clinical procedure has been belied by its poor record.

He also pointed to autopsies that show that, despite the relative sterility of the procedure, prisoners still experience pain.

Critics say such information calls into question the widespread use of lethal injection and whether it should be discarded altogether.

“Lethal injection, from the very start, was about a humane-looking execution, not a humane execution,” said Lain, the law professor. “There’s a big difference.”

articles.title: 'This is emergency': 10,000 detained across India ahead of Delhi's Jantar Mantar stir, says CJP
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: At least 10,000 people have been detained across the country ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) planned protest at Jantar Mantar in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: At least 10,000 people have been detained across the country ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) planned protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on October 10, the party's spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed on Friday.The CJP said those detained included students from Pune who were travelling to Delhi to participate in the protest. According to the party, the students were being taken away in a bus to an unknown location.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned the restrictions on the planned demonstration, responding to a video of activists being detained with the remark: "Why not just declare EMERGENCY?" (sic)"At least 10000 people have been detained across the country across (Cockroach Janta Party), various student orgs, Kisaan and Dalit Sangathans, political parties. THIS IS EMERGENCY," Ranka said in a post on X. (sic)Among those detained was national spokesperson Deepak Baliyan, who was taken into police custody on Thursday and released later that night, the party said.The detentions came ahead of the CJP's planned march to Jantar Mantar to demand the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and accountability for the alleged deletion of voters.\Dipke had called for a nationwide mobilisation against the exercise, saying the protest would proceed even if the party's leaders were detained or arrested.Addressing a press conference on Thursday, he criticised restrictions on public gatherings in the national capital and questioned why protests could be held in Mumbai and Bengaluru but not in Delhi."Jantar Mantar belongs to people of India, it does not belong to Union Home Minister Amit Shah," he said."If Mumbai and Bengaluru can have peaceful protests, why is Amit Shah not allowing it in Delhi?" the CJP founder asked.Dipke urged political parties, civil society groups and social activists to unite to protect voting rights. He alleged that large numbers of voters had been deleted from electoral rolls and questioned the Election Commission's role in the exercise."SIR is the biggest scam that the central government, the BJP-ruled government, is pulling off to kill democracy in India," he said.Referring to testimonies of people allegedly declared dead in electoral records despite producing Aadhaar, PAN and other valid documents to establish that they were alive, Dipke questioned how living voters could be marked dead and removed from the rolls.He alleged that the BJP and the Election Commission were working together to delete the votes of people who did not support the ruling party. The Election Commission's role and the allegations made by the CJP could not be independently established from the party's claims.Dipke also cited alleged deletions in constituencies associated with opposition leaders, including former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, Tamil Nadu chief minister M K Stalin and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal. He questioned whether the cases were coincidental or pointed to a pattern."If we believe that there is no involvement of the BJP with the Election Commission, then why is it always the opposition leaders who lose? And why does it always benefit the BJP?" he asked.He described the process as "unconstitutional", arguing that it undermined the principle that people should choose their government rather than the government determining who could vote."The government is selecting who will be the voter and who will not vote," he said.The CJP founder said the October 10 march would seek to hold Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Centre accountable for the alleged deletion of votes. He also urged Delhi Police to learn from Karnataka Police how to protect people's rights.Dipke criticised PM Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah, saying they did not own the country or Jantar Mantar and were only "servants with a fixed tenure to serve people".He said the party was not seeking to destabilise the country but wanted accountability over the alleged electoral irregularities.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das alleged that party members and young participants in the movement were facing "mass detentions" in several states, including Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Delhi."None of us are afraid of arrests or detentions. The protest has to go on with or without us," he said.Actor Prakash Raj, who addressed a gathering in Bengaluru earlier, said civil society organisations in Karnataka had spent nearly a year documenting alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise and had presented their findings in different parts of the country.He said testimonies presented at a tribunal, including those of people allegedly declared dead in electoral records, showed that the issue extended beyond Karnataka.Raj appealed to the media to focus on SIR and expressed solidarity with young protesters travelling to Delhi for the October 10 demonstration. He said Karnataka's civil society groups also supported them.He added that the movement had grown from a Karnataka-based campaign into a broader national struggle, thanking the organisations and young activists involved in documenting alleged irregularities and bringing affected voters before the tribunal.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: ICE shooting of New York man in car with five-year-old sparks protests
articles.summary: Mayor, governor and US lawmakers condemn the shooting by immigration officers.
articles.body:
An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent has shot a man in New York City as he sat in a car with a child.

Citing an “unconscionable and incredibly serious situation”, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said early reports indicated that agents surrounded the man and a five-year-old in his car on Thursday in the Marble Hill neighbourhood before firing multiple rounds.

The child was believed to be physically unharmed, the mayor added as he said he has called United States President Donald Trump and would demand that he end all ICE enforcement actions in the city.

“I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorise our communities,” Mamdani said.

Protests followed on Thursday evening with demonstrators saying the shooting illustrated the dangers of Trump’s immigration crackdown, and some scuffles with police broke out.

“We are heartbroken and enraged,” said City Council member Carmen De La Rosa, who represents the area.

Speaking at the scene in the evening, Mamdani said: “Today’s shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known, which is that ICE operates with impunity, that they sow chaos and terror across our country, that they have killed far more of our neighbours than they could ever have claimed to save.”

He demanded the agency “must be abolished”.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul said she spoke with Trump and US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Thursday night.

“I expressed outrage on behalf of New Yorkers and urged them to halt ICE enforcement operations in New York,” she said in a statement.

“I also asked that any body camera footage of the shooting be released to the public, so we can establish the facts and get to the truth.”

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, said its officers were conducting a “targeted enforcement operation” in the Bronx about 4pm to arrest a 28-year-old Dominican national with a criminal conviction identified as Oscar Belgal by city police.

It said an officer “discharged his weapon” and “the criminal illegal alien” was injured. The DHS added that the incident remains under investigation.

Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said Belgal was pulling into a parking space when a federal officer in plain clothes approached with a gun drawn, followed by another federal officer who also wasn’t in uniform.

Belgal started to pull the car forward, and then at least one of the officers fired seven rounds, hitting the man below his left ear, Tisch said, confirming that the child was unharmed and was with a relative.

According to a statement by the New York Police Department, the man remained conscious and was receiving medical treatment at a nearby hospital.

The shooting took place after months of mounting criticism of the agency.

In January, federal immigration agents shot dead two US citizens in Minneapolis: Renee Nicole Good, a 37-year-old mother of three, killed by an ICE agent on January 7, and Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old intensive care nurse, shot by a US border agent.

After Good’s killing, Trump officials labelled her a “domestic terrorist” even as video of the shooting cast doubt on their claims she had tried to run over an agent.

The federal government removed local authorities from the investigation, rejected calls for a civil rights probe and sent hundreds more agents to Minnesota, bringing the total to 3,000, as protests against the killings and the immigration crackdown spread to hundreds of US cities.

Trump blamed the shift in US opinion about the immigration agency on unfair media coverage, urging DHS and ICE to publicise the “violent criminals” they arrest.

ICE has been tasked with deporting one million people a year.

The agency doubled in size in the first year of the second Trump administration to more than 22,000 agents by January and is now the highest-funded federal law enforcement agency with about $75bn allocated to it over four years under a tax bill Trump signed last year.

articles.title: US plans to livestream Fort Hood shooter’s death; first public execution in 90 years
articles.summary: The Pentagon has announced that it will livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, the former Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13
articles.body: The Pentagon has announced that it will livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, the former Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009. The execution is scheduled for December 3 at the Texas military base where Hasan carried out the shooting.A Pentagon official confirmed the livestream to Reuters on Thursday, saying, “It will be livestreamed. Details will follow.” Defence secretary Pete Hegseth also confirmed the plan in a post on X, a day after saying the execution would be “public”.Hasan is set to become the first person executed by a US military firing squad since 1945. The Army announced earlier this week that the execution would take place at Fort Hood, where Hasan opened fire in a medical facility on November 5, 2009, killing 13 people and injuring 32 others.Hegseth, who championed the decision to execute Hasan by firing squad, said the public should be able to watch the execution because people needed to understand that such crimes carried “serious consequences”. He told the conservative programme Human Events Daily that scheduling the execution at Fort Hood on a Thursday at 1 pm, around the time and day of the original shooting, was a “no-brainer”.Asked whether Hasan had made any final requests, Hegseth said, “Don’t care. We’ll see him on December 3.”The decision has raised questions about the legal and ethical implications of broadcasting an execution, particularly as the US faces renewed scrutiny over capital punishment following a botched lethal injection in Tennessee last week.Media organisations have sought to televise US executions in the past but have been blocked by courts. Reuters reported that experts were unaware of any other country currently televising or livestreaming a legally sanctioned execution. Public executions have become rare worldwide, although Iran and Taliban-run Afghanistan have conducted them in recent years.The last legally sanctioned public execution in the US took place in 1936, when thousands watched the hanging of a Black man convicted of raping a white woman, according to death penalty experts cited by Reuters.Experts question the need for a public executionLegal experts have raised concerns about the purpose of livestreaming Hasan’s execution and whether it could face a legal challenge.Eugene Fidell, a military law expert and visiting lecturer at Yale Law School, told the Associated Press that Hasan could seek to delay the execution by filing a habeas petition in civilian court, challenging the legality of his detention. Fidell also told Reuters that livestreaming an execution would be “extremely, extremely strange” and that Hasan would need to sue in federal court if he wanted to block the public broadcast.The US Supreme Court has never directly addressed the question of livestreaming an execution, Fidell told Reuters, leaving open questions about how courts might approach such a challenge.Elisabeth Semel, co-director of the Death Penalty Clinic at UC Berkeley Law, told the Associated Press that the decision raised questions about the condemned prisoner’s dignity, who would be allowed to view the broadcast and what the administration hoped to achieve through the spectacle.“This is a president who’s about spectacle and that’s, I think, precisely the message that he intends to deliver,” Semel said, referring to president Donald Trump.Other experts said the debate over livestreaming came at a time when states were struggling to carry out lethal injections because of difficulties obtaining drugs and finding medical professionals willing to participate in executions.Trump approves execution amid scrutiny of death penaltyUnder US military law, the president must approve an execution by firing squad. Trump authorised Hasan’s execution on Hegseth’s recommendation, the Pentagon said earlier this week. The White House referred questions about the livestream to the Pentagon and did not say whether Trump supported broadcasting it.A military jury sentenced Hasan to death in August 2013 after finding him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted premeditated murder. He was 39 at the time of the attack and was scheduled to deploy to Afghanistan weeks later. He was shot by law enforcement during his arrest, leaving him partially paralysed and confined to a wheelchair.Hasan represented himself at trial after dismissing his lawyers, acknowledged that he was the gunman and did little to mount a defence. He said he had acted to prevent soldiers from going to Afghanistan and killing fellow Muslims, but a military judge barred him from presenting that argument as a defence.It remains unclear whether Hasan will challenge the execution.The case has also brought renewed attention to the methods used to carry out the death penalty in the US. At least five states permit firing squads, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. South Carolina carried out the first firing squad execution in the US in 15 years in 2025.The Trump administration has also expanded the methods permitted for federal executions to include firing squads, electrocution and gas asphyxiation, partly because of difficulties obtaining lethal-injection drugs.You use AI every day. articles.title: South Korea to recall its ambassador to Ukraine over North Korean POW dispute
articles.summary: President Lee Jae Myung had threatened punitive measures unless Ukraine apologized for revealing the transfer of two North Korean prisoners.
articles.body: SEOUL, South Korea — South Korea said Thursday that it would recall its ambassador to Ukraine, stepping up its protest against Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s recent revelation of a supposedly secret transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea. The South Korean announcement came days after President Lee Jae Myung threatened to take unspecified punitive steps if Ukraine refuses to apologize over the revelation. South Korea’s Foreign Ministry did not say when the ambassador, Park Ki-chang, will be brought back home. A ministry statement said that South Korea would continue consultations with Ukraine, adding that it hoped the dispute between the two countries would be resolved smoothly. Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi said Ukraine remains open to “constructive dialogue” despite Seoul’s decision to recall its ambassador. “Diplomacy must prevail over emotions,” he said, according to local media outlet RBC-Ukraine. South Korea and Ukraine became embroiled in a diplomatic dispute after Zelenskyy spoke about the transfer of the North Korean soldiers during his U.N. speech on Sept. 23. South Korea has accused Ukraine of violating a nondisclosure agreement on their transfer in mid-September, but Kyiv has denied agreeing to such a deal. The soldiers were among thousands of North Korean troops deployed to support Russia’s war against Ukraine. Since their capture in early 2025, the soldiers had expressed their desires to resettle in South Korea, because they could face persecution if repatriated. South Korea had said it would accept them, because it legally regards the North as part of its territory and has a policy of accepting and financially supporting North Korean defectors. South Korean officials said the nondisclosure agreement was made because they were concerned about the safety of the North Korean soldiers and their relatives in the North. But many experts say South Korea’s liberal government is likely also worried that the disclosure of their arrival may hurt its efforts to improve ties with North Korea. North Korean state media have not commented on the soldiers’ transfer. But the North previously reacted with fury to major defections of its citizens, accusing South Korea of kidnapping them. North Korea has shunned any talks with South Korea and the United States and focused on bolstering its nuclear program since 2019. It is unclear what other steps South Korea would take. Experts say maintaining good relations with Ukraine is in South Korean national interests because Kyiv could provide Seoul with intelligence about North Korea’s expanding cooperation with Russia and its battlefield experiences. They say cooperation with Ukraine is important for South Korea’s partnerships with many Western countries supporting Ukraine over the war. Observers say Zelenskyy disclosed the transfer of the North Korean POWs to expose the danger of North Korea’s military support to Russia as a way to win more international assistance. South Korea has provided $445 million in humanitarian assistance to Ukraine since 2022. In July, Lee pledged $100 million in aid to Ukraine in a meeting with Zelenskyy.

articles.title: Laotian man deported by U.S. to South Sudan leaves for Laos after year in detention
articles.summary: Thongxay Nilakout, 49, had been willing to return to Laos before the U.S. deported him to South Sudan, attorney Tin Nguyen said.
articles.body: JUBA, South Sudan — A Laotian man deported by the United States to South Sudan left for Laos on Thursday after spending more than a year in detention in Africa, an ordeal his attorney said could have been avoided. Thongxay Nilakout, 49, had been willing to return to Laos before the U.S. deported him to South Sudan, attorney Tin Nguyen said. A Lao consular officer had told his family that a travel document had already been issued. Nilakout left South Sudan on Thursday afternoon for Vientiane, the capital of Laos, Nguyen said. He had been detained in Juba, South Sudan’s capital, since July 2025. South Sudan’s Foreign Ministry said Thursday that it had coordinated his repatriation with the government of Laos, which provided assurances against torture or other ill treatment upon his return. “Thongxay’s deportation to Laos is not just a relief for his family, it is proof of what we argued from day one. He should have been sent to Laos,” Nguyen said in a statement. The U.S. Department of Homeland Security said it was preparing a response to questions about Nilakout’s case and requested more time to comment. Nilakout and seven other men were sent to Africa in May 2025, rerouted first to a U.S. military base in Djibouti after a federal judge blocked their deportation to South Sudan midflight. They arrived in Juba aboard a military aircraft after a Supreme Court ruling allowed their removal. The eight were held in a gated house under armed guard. All had criminal convictions in the U.S. but had served their prison sentences before being taken into immigration custody. Hundreds have been deported from the U.S. to African countries that aren’t their home nations, according to advocacy groups Human Rights First and Refugees International, which have been monitoring the deportations. Around a dozen African countries have accepted third-country deportees from the U.S., some in exchange for millions of dollars in payments, though details of the South Sudan deal remain murky. The choice of South Sudan was particularly controversial given its poor human rights record and political instability. Armed conflict displaced more than half a million people there in 2025, according to the United Nations. Nilakout resettled in the U.S. as a child in 1980 after his family fled Laos, spending time first in a refugee camp in Thailand, his attorney said. In 1995, he was sentenced to life in prison without parole for his role in the murder of a German tourist during an armed robbery in Southern California. He was 17 at the time of the crime. His attorney said he became eligible for parole after a 2012 U.S. Supreme Court ruling found mandatory life sentences without parole for juvenile offenders unconstitutional. He was released in 2023 and was working as a restaurant cook when U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement took him into custody in March 2025. Four of the original eight deportees remain in South Sudan, including two Burmese nationals and two Cuban nationals. A Congolese national deported separately has since joined them, bringing the total to five, Nguyen said. South Sudan’s Foreign Ministry confirmed that five third-country deportees remain in South Sudan and said it was working with the governments concerned and international partners to facilitate their safe and humane repatriation.
